verses.original: Ἰάκωβος δοῦλος Θεοῦ καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ Ταῖς δώδεκα φυλαῖς ταῖς ἐν τῇ Διασπορᾷ Χαίρειν
verses.transliteration: Iakōbos doulos Theou kai Kyriou Iēsou Christou Tais dōdeka phylais tais en tē Diaspora Chairein
verses.literal: James a servant of God and of [the] Lord Jesus Christ To the twelve tribes - of the Dispersion Greetings

verses.original: ἡγήσασθε Πᾶσαν χαρὰν μου ἀδελφοί ὅταν περιπέσητε πειρασμοῖς ποικίλοις
verses.transliteration: hēgēsasthe Pasan charan mou adelphoi hotan peripesēte peirasmois poikilois
verses.literal: Consider [it] pure joy my brothers when you encounter trials of many kinds

verses.original: γινώσκοντες ὅτι τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως κατεργάζεται ὑπομονήν
verses.transliteration: ginōskontes hoti to dokimion hymōn tēs pisteōs katergazetai hypomonēn
verses.literal: because you know that the testing of your - faith develops perseverance

verses.original: δὲ ἐχέτω ἡ ὑπομονὴ τέλειον ἔργον ἵνα ἦτε τέλειοι καὶ ὁλόκληροι λειπόμενοι ἐν μηδενὶ
verses.transliteration: de echetō hē hypomonē teleion ergon hina ēte teleioi kai holoklēroi leipomenoi en mēdeni
verses.literal: - Allow - perseverance to finish [its] work so that you may be mature and complete [not] lacking - [anything]

verses.original: δέ Εἰ τις ὑμῶν λείπεται σοφίας αἰτείτω παρὰ Θεοῦ τοῦ διδόντος ἁπλῶς πᾶσιν καὶ μὴ ὀνειδίζοντος καὶ δοθήσεται αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: de Ei tis hymōn leipetai sophias aiteitō para Theou tou didontos haplōs pasin kai mē oneidizontos kai dothēsetai autō
verses.literal: Now if any of you lacks wisdom he should ask . . . God who gives generously to all - without finding fault and it will be given to him

verses.original: δὲ αἰτείτω ἐν πίστει μηδὲν διακρινόμενος γὰρ ὁ διακρινόμενος ἔοικεν κλύδωνι θαλάσσης ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ
verses.transliteration: de aiteitō en pistei mēden diakrinomenos gar ho diakrinomenos eoiken klydōni thalassēs anemizomenō kai rhipizomenō
verses.literal: But he must ask in faith without doubting because he who doubts is like a wave of [the] sea blown and tossed by the wind

verses.original: γὰρ ἐκεῖνος ὁ ἄνθρωπος μὴ οἰέσθω ὅτι λήμψεταί τι παρὰ τοῦ Κυρίου
verses.transliteration: gar ekeinos ho anthrōpos mē oiesthō hoti lēmpsetai ti para tou Kyriou
verses.literal: - That - man {should} not expect - to receive anything from the Lord

verses.original: δίψυχος ἀνὴρ ἀκατάστατος ἐν πάσαις αὐτοῦ ταῖς ὁδοῖς
verses.transliteration: dipsychos anēr akatastatos en pasais autou tais hodois
verses.literal: [He is] a double-minded man unstable in all his - ways

verses.original: δὲ ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς Καυχάσθω ἐν αὐτοῦ τῷ ὕψει
verses.transliteration: de ho adelphos ho tapeinos Kauchasthō en autou tō hypsei
verses.literal: - The brother - in humble circumstances should exult in his - high position

verses.original: δὲ ὁ πλούσιος ἐν αὐτοῦ τῇ ταπεινώσει ὅτι παρελεύσεται ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου
verses.transliteration: de ho plousios en autou tē tapeinōsei hoti pareleusetai hōs anthos chortou
verses.literal: But the [one who is] rich [should exult] in his - low position because he will pass away like a flower of the field

verses.original: γὰρ ὁ ἥλιος ἀνέτειλεν σὺν τῷ καύσωνι καὶ ἐξήρανεν τὸν χόρτον καὶ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἄνθος ἐξέπεσεν καὶ ἡ εὐπρέπεια αὐτοῦ τοῦ προσώπου ἀπώλετο οὕτως καὶ ὁ πλούσιος μαρανθήσεται ἐν αὐτοῦ ταῖς πορείαις
verses.transliteration: gar ho hēlios aneteilen syn tō kausōni kai exēranen ton chorton kai autou to anthos exepesen kai hē euprepeia autou tou prosōpou apōleto houtōs kai ho plousios maranthēsetai en autou tais poreiais
verses.literal: For the sun rises with - scorching heat and withers the plant - its - flower falls and [its] beauty . . . . . . . . . is lost So too the rich [man] will fade away in the midst of his - pursuits

verses.original: Μακάριος ἀνὴρ ὃς ὑπομένει πειρασμόν ὅτι γενόμενος δόκιμος λήμψεται τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς ὃν ἐπηγγείλατο τοῖς ἀγαπῶσιν αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Makarios anēr hos hypomenei peirasmon hoti genomenos dokimos lēmpsetai ton stephanon tēs zōēs hon epēngeilato tois agapōsin auton
verses.literal: Blessed [is the] man who perseveres under trial because when he has stood the test he will receive the crown - of life that [God] has promised to those who love Him

verses.original: πειραζόμενος Μηδεὶς λεγέτω ὅτι Ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πειράζομαι γὰρ ὁ Θεὸς ἐστιν ἀπείραστός κακῶν δὲ αὐτὸς πειράζει οὐδένα
verses.transliteration: peirazomenos Mēdeis legetō hoti Apo Theou peirazomai gar ho Theos estin apeirastos kakōn de autos peirazei oudena
verses.literal: When tempted no one should say - vvv God is tempting me For - God vvv cannot be tempted by evil [nor] vvv does He tempt [anyone]

verses.original: δὲ ἕκαστος πειράζεται ὑπὸ τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἐξελκόμενος καὶ δελεαζόμενος
verses.transliteration: de hekastos peirazetai hypo tēs idias epithymias exelkomenos kai deleazomenos
verses.literal: But each one is tempted [when] by [his] own evil desires he is lured away and enticed

verses.original: εἶτα ἡ ἐπιθυμία συλλαβοῦσα τίκτει ἁμαρτίαν δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία ἀποτελεσθεῖσα ἀποκύει θάνατον
verses.transliteration: eita hē epithymia syllabousa tiktei hamartian de hē hamartia apotelestheisa apokyei thanaton
verses.literal: Then - [after] desire has conceived it gives birth to sin and - sin when it is full-grown gives birth to death

verses.original: Μὴ πλανᾶσθε μου ἀγαπητοί ἀδελφοί
verses.transliteration: Mē planasthe mou agapētoi adelphoi
verses.literal: {Do} not be deceived my beloved brothers

verses.original: πᾶσα ἀγαθὴ δόσις καὶ πᾶν τέλειον δώρημα ἐστιν ἄνωθέν καταβαῖνον ἀπὸ τοῦ Πατρὸς τῶν φώτων παρ’ ᾧ ἔνι οὐκ παραλλαγὴ ἢ τροπῆς ἀποσκίασμα
verses.transliteration: pasa agathē dosis kai pan teleion dōrēma estin anōthen katabainon apo tou Patros tōn phōtōn par’ hō eni ouk parallagē ē tropēs aposkiasma
verses.literal: Every vvv good and - perfect gift is from above coming down from the Father - of the heavenly lights with whom there is no change or shifting shadow

verses.original: βουληθεὶς ἀπεκύησεν ἡμᾶς λόγῳ ἀληθείας εἰς ἡμᾶς τὸ εἶναι τινα ἀπαρχήν αὐτοῦ τῶν κτισμάτων
verses.transliteration: boulētheis apekyēsen hēmas logō alētheias eis hēmas to einai tina aparchēn autou tōn ktismatōn
verses.literal: He chose to give us birth . . . through [the] word of truth that we - would be a kind of firstfruits of His - creation

verses.original: μου ἀγαπητοί ἀδελφοί Ἴστε δὲ πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ἔστω ταχὺς εἰς τὸ ἀκοῦσαι βραδὺς εἰς τὸ λαλῆσαι βραδὺς εἰς ὀργήν
verses.transliteration: mou agapētoi adelphoi Iste de pas anthrōpos estō tachys eis to akousai bradys eis to lalēsai bradys eis orgēn
verses.literal: My beloved brothers understand this - Everyone . . . should be quick to - listen slow to - speak [and] slow to anger

verses.original: γὰρ ἀνδρὸς ὀργὴ οὐκ ἐργάζεται δικαιοσύνην Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: gar andros orgē ouk ergazetai dikaiosynēn Theou
verses.literal: for man’s anger {does} not bring about [the] righteousness that God [desires]

verses.original: διὸ ἀποθέμενοι πᾶσαν ῥυπαρίαν καὶ περισσείαν κακίας ἐν πραΰτητι δέξασθε τὸν λόγον ἔμφυτον τὸν δυνάμενον σῶσαι ὑμῶν τὰς ψυχὰς
verses.transliteration: dio apothemenoi pasan rhyparian kai perisseian kakias en prautēti dexasthe ton logon emphyton ton dynamenon sōsai hymōn tas psychas
verses.literal: Therefore get rid of all moral filth and every expression of evil vvv [and] humbly accept the word planted [in you] which can save your - souls

verses.original: δὲ Γίνεσθε ποιηταὶ λόγου καὶ μὴ ἀκροαταὶ μόνον παραλογιζόμενοι ἑαυτούς
verses.transliteration: de Ginesthe poiētai logou kai mē akroatai monon paralogizomenoi heautous
verses.literal: - Be doers of [the] word and not hearers only [Otherwise,] you are deceiving yourselves

verses.original: ὅτι εἴ τις ἐστὶν ἀκροατὴς λόγου καὶ οὐ ποιητής οὗτος ἔοικεν ἀνδρὶ κατανοοῦντι τὸ τῆς αὐτοῦ γενέσεως πρόσωπον ἐν ἐσόπτρῳ
verses.transliteration: hoti ei tis estin akroatēs logou kai ou poiētēs houtos eoiken andri katanoounti to tēs autou geneseōs prosōpon en esoptrō
verses.literal: For - anyone vvv who hears [the] word but vvv does not carry it out - is like a man [who] looks - - at his vvv face in a mirror

verses.original: γὰρ κατενόησεν ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀπελήλυθεν καὶ εὐθέως ἐπελάθετο ὁποῖος ἦν
verses.transliteration: gar katenoēsen heauton kai apelēlythen kai eutheōs epelatheto hopoios ēn
verses.literal: [and] after observing himself - goes away and immediately forgets vvv what he [looks] like

verses.original: δὲ ὁ παρακύψας εἰς τέλειον νόμον τὸν τῆς ἐλευθερίας καὶ παραμείνας οὐκ γενόμενος ἐπιλησμονῆς ἀκροατὴς ἀλλὰ ἔργου ποιητὴς οὗτος ἔσται μακάριος ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ ποιήσει
verses.transliteration: de ho parakypsas eis teleion nomon ton tēs eleutherias kai parameinas ouk genomenos epilēsmonēs akroatēs alla ergou poiētēs houtos estai makarios en tē autou poiēsei
verses.literal: But the [one who] looks intently into [the] perfect law - - of freedom and continues to do so not being a forgetful hearer but an effective doer [he] will be blessed in what he does

verses.original: Εἴ τις δοκεῖ εἶναι θρησκὸς μὴ χαλιναγωγῶν αὐτοῦ γλῶσσαν ἀλλὰ ἀπατῶν αὐτοῦ καρδίαν τούτου ἡ θρησκεία μάταιος
verses.transliteration: Ei tis dokei einai thrēskos mē chalinagōgōn autou glōssan alla apatōn autou kardian toutou hē thrēskeia mataios
verses.literal: If anyone considers himself . . . religious vvv [and yet] does not bridle his tongue - he deceives his heart [and his] - religion [is] worthless

verses.original: καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος θρησκεία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ ἐστίν αὕτη ἐπισκέπτεσθαι ὀρφανοὺς καὶ χήρας ἐν αὐτῶν τῇ θλίψει τηρεῖν ἑαυτὸν ἄσπιλον ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου
verses.transliteration: kathara kai amiantos thrēskeia para tō Theō kai Patri estin hautē episkeptesthai orphanous kai chēras en autōn tē thlipsei tērein heauton aspilon apo tou kosmou
verses.literal: Pure and undefiled religion before [our] God and Father is this to care for orphans and widows in their - distress [and] to keep oneself from being polluted by the world
